message.content:
Good, now working on eng-2219.
Findings

Medium

1. apps/roam/src/utils/materializeSharedNode.ts:370 — assets are uploaded before both title-collision guards, so a failed import permanently orphans blobs in the user's Roam storage.
The asset stage runs at line 370, before createImportedPage's collision guard (:178) and updateImportedPage's (:243), and before the writeImportedSourceIdentity failure path (:206-225) that deletes the page it just created. Scenario: a user imports a shared node whose title matches an existing local page. Nothing is imported, they are told to "Rename or remove that page, then import again", and N blobs are now permanently in their graph with no Roam API to list or delete them. mirrorAssetToRoamStorage.ts documents the copy as irrevocable and treats an orphaned upload as the cost to avoid. Both checks are synchronous and cheap; they belong above the importNodeAssets call.

2. apps/roam/src/utils/materializeSharedNode.ts:391 — AssetImportReport has no consumer, so the documented degradation is silent end to end.
importSharedNodes.ts:35-41 maps the result down to { sharedNode, status } and drops result.assets; refreshImportedNode.ts:68-73 returns only Refreshed "<title>" from <space>; DiscoverSharedNodesDialog.tsx:243-274 only surfaces isFailedSharedNodeImport. Scenario: a node with a 7 MB image imports, mirrorAssetToRoamStorage returns skipped/too-large, the token attachments/diagram.png stays in the page, and the user is told the import succeeded with no indication anything degraded. The result-shape half of the requirement is met; the reporting half is not wired through. Either surface it or note in the type that it is currently unread.

Low

3. apps/roam/src/utils/importNodeAssets.ts:37, :105, :117, :127 — EMPTY_REPORT is a shared mutable module constant handed out to callers.
Lines 105 and 127 return the constant itself, so every asset-free node in a session shares one object identity; line 117's { ...EMPTY_REPORT, failed: [...] } still aliases EMPTY_REPORT.skipped. The moment anything aggregates reports (finding 2) with report.failed.push(...), one node's failure is retroactively attributed to every other node. Build a fresh report per path, or Object.freeze the constant.

4. apps/roam/src/utils/importNodeAssets.ts:140 — mirrored/reused count references, not distinct hashes.
Two references to identical bytes within one node report mirrored: 1, reused: 1, contradicting the field's own doc ("Already held by this graph, so no upload was needed"). The second was uploaded by this same run. A user seeing reused: 1 on a first-ever import will read it as a cache hit from a previous one.

5. apps/roam/src/utils/importNodeAssets.ts:140 — every recorded reference is downloaded and uploaded whether or not its token occurs in the fetched markdown.
rewriteAssetLinks is the only thing that consults the text, and it runs after all uploads. Two ways rows outlive their tokens: publishNodeAssets.removeUnreferencedAssets is best-effort (publishNodeAssets.ts:127 logs and continues), so a stale row survives a publish whose cleanup failed; and fetchFullMarkdown strips frontmatter (Obsidian) or the title heading (Roam) at materializeSharedNode.ts:160-165 while publication recorded references from the unstripped content, so a frontmatter-only asset has a row and no token. Either way the importer permanently spends storage on a blob the page never renders, and report.mirrored is inflated. A markdown.includes(...) pre-filter using lookupCandidates' decoded form would make the upload set match the rewrite set.

6. apps/roam/src/utils/importNodeAssets.ts:9 — the module docstring's degradation claim holds only for Roam-origin tokens.
"Leaves its token exactly as published, which still renders wherever the publishing platform's URL was public" is true for a Firebase URL. An Obsidian-origin token is a vault path, and the wikilink spellings rewriteAssetLinks matches (![[attachments/diagram.png]]) are left verbatim in a Roam page, where [[...]] is a page reference — so a failed or oversized Obsidian asset silently creates junk pages named after vault paths in the user's graph. Narrow the comment, or degrade Obsidian wikilink tokens to plain text.

7. apps/roam/src/utils/materializeSharedNode.ts:370 — the asset stage is the only awaited step without a failure guard.
Every other step is wrapped into a typed MaterializationFailure with a stage; this await is bare. Inside, the reference query (importNodeAssets.ts:113-126) and each mirror call (:164) are guarded, but rewriteAssetLinks(...) at :172 is not, nor is a synchronous throw from client.from(...). That contradicts the header's "Nothing here can fail the node": such a throw exits materializeSharedNode as a stage-less rejection, caught only by the generic handlers at importSharedNodes.ts:43 and refreshImportedNode.ts:76.

8. apps/roam/src/utils/importNodeAssets.ts:143-162 — ResolvedAsset.mimetype is left unset even though the mirror step knows it.
mirrorAssetToRoamStorage computes info?.contentType || blob.type for the upload filename but does not return it, so resolved.push({ sourceRef, url, sourcePath }) cannot populate it. rewriteAssetLinks.ts names mimetype as its highest-fidelity signal and calls out the exact unresolved case: a Roam-origin storage URL with no recorded source_path renders as a labelled link with a uid for a label instead of the right embed. Threading it through MirroredAsset closes the gap (partially — ReusedAsset comes from the registry and has none).

9. apps/roam/src/utils/importNodeAssets.ts:49-57 — duplicated getErrorMessage.
materializeSharedNode.ts:77 already exports one, imported by both importSharedNodes.ts and refreshImportedNode.ts. The local copy differs only by also reading message off a bare Postgrest object — a strictly better implementation. Promote the superset rather than shadowing it.

Verified clean

Failed and oversized assets are correctly excluded from resolved, so their tokens survive verbatim (importNodeAssets.ts:145-156). The sequential loop honours mirrorAssetToRoamStorage's "one asset at a time" contract, and both production callers drive nodes sequentially, so no Promise.all breaks it. Re-sync does not re-upload: readMirroredAssetUrl is a synchronous Datalog read and recordMirroredAsset is awaited before the mirror returns. The stage is genuinely origin-agnostic — it iterates rows and never inspects token shape — and the my_file_references columns and space_id/source_local_id filter match the view in packages/database/supabase/schemas/assets.sql:30 and the generated types, with the same nullable-column defensiveness as publishNodeAssets.ts:78-88. All 38 tests across the three suites pass locally.

---

Finding 1 is the one I'd act on first — it's an unrecoverable side effect on a path the code otherwise treats as a clean no-op, and the fix is just moving the collision checks above the stage. Findings 2 and 6 both touch the ticket's stated degradation contract. Nothing was modified; say the word if you want any of these applied.

**Finding 1 fixed.** `tsc --noEmit` clean; 34 files / 294 tests pass.

Extracted `titleCollisionFailure`, called from `materializeSharedNode` immediately after `fetch-content` and before `importNodeAssets`. Both import paths still call it — the message belongs with the check rather than duplicated at the call site, and they're exported behaviour in their own right. Two synchronous reads, so the early check costs nothing. Both existing collision tests now assert `from` was never called with `my_file_references`, which is exactly what would have failed before the move.

Triage on the rest, with two corrections:

**Finding 2 is explicitly out of scope for this ticket.** ENG-2219's Out of Scope reads: *"Showing failures to the user. ENG-1877 covers that."* So the right action is the reviewer's second option — a line on `AssetImportReport` saying it is deliberately unread pending ENG-1877 — not wiring it through the dialog.

**Finding 9's suggested direction creates a cycle.** `materializeSharedNode` imports `importNodeAssets`, so `importNodeAssets` can't import `getErrorMessage` back from it. The superset needs to move to a neutral module that both import.

The rest as I'd rank them:

| # | Verdict |
|---|---|
| 3 | Fix — `EMPTY_REPORT` aliasing is a live trap the moment anything aggregates; freeze or build fresh |
| 7 | Fix — wrap the stage in the same typed failure as its neighbours; cheap and it makes the header comment true |
| 4 | Fix — count distinct hashes within the run, not references |
| 5 | Fix, slightly larger — pre-filter on `markdown.includes` over the decoded candidates; needs `lookupCandidates` exported from `rewriteAssetLinks` |
| 6 | Narrow the comment. The stronger half (degrading wikilinks to plain text) contradicts the spec's "leave that reference token unchanged", so the junk-page risk wants a ticket, not a silent behaviour change |
| 8 | Fix, but note it edits `mirrorAssetToRoamStorage.ts` — that's ENG-2218's file, so the change lands in 2219's diff |

Say which of those you want and I'll work through them.

content.text:
All five done. `tsc --noEmit` clean, 34 files / 298 tests pass. Diff is confined to the two stage files, `rewriteAssetLinks` (one export), and two test files.

**3 — `EMPTY_REPORT` aliasing.** Replaced with `emptyReport()`, a fresh object per path, including the `{ ...emptyReport(), failed: [...] }` case that was aliasing `skipped`. Test: two asset-free imports, push onto the first's `failed`, assert the second's is still empty.

**7 — unguarded stage.** Wrapped in the same `failure(...)` shape as its neighbours, under a new `copy-assets` stage.

This one corrected me mid-way. I wrote a test asserting a synchronous throw from `client.from("my_file_references")` surfaces as `stage: "copy-assets"` — it failed, because `fetchNodeReferences` is *already* inside `importNodeAssets`'s try/catch, so that throw degrades into a reported failure rather than rejecting. The finding's "nor is a synchronous throw from `client.from(...)`" is wrong on that point. I removed the test rather than reshape it around a mock, and rewrote my comment to say what the guard actually covers: the link rewrite, and whatever a later edit adds outside those guards. It's cheap insurance, not a fix for a reachable path — worth knowing before it reads as tested behaviour.

**4 — counts.** A `handledHashes` set means counts are per distinct blob. Test: two tokens, one hash, mirror returning `mirrored` then `reused` → report says `mirrored: 1, reused: 0`, not `1/1`.

**5 — uploading references the markdown never makes.** Filtered before the loop. This needed a second pass: `lookupCandidates` widens markdown→row by *decoding*, but the filter goes row→markdown and needs the *encoded* spelling. A test with a recorded `my folder/d.png` against `![](my%20folder/d.png)` caught it; added `spellingsOf`, which adds `encodeURI(filepath)` on top of the candidates. `lookupCandidates` is now exported. Two tests: a reference absent from the body is never mirrored, and a percent-encoded one still is.

**6 — docstring.** Narrowed. It now says the benign case is Roam-origin only, and states the Obsidian consequence outright: `![[attachments/diagram.png]]` left verbatim is a page reference, so a failed Obsidian asset leaves a link to an empty page named after a vault path. It also says why this stage doesn't fix it — the contract requires the unresolved token to survive unchanged, which is what lets a later re-import resolve it.

That junk-page behaviour is a real user-visible defect with no home. Want me to draft a ticket for it?

Every bullet above is placeholder guidance. Replace or remove every placeholder before presenting a draft or creating a ticket. Keep all five headings, leaving `Out of Scope` or `Notes` empty when nothing useful applies. Use 1–3 short bullets per section unless the ticket is genuinely complex.

## Ticket readiness

Always use the Engineering team. This skill never creates or redirects to Feedback.

- Use `Backlog` when the problem is known, the fix is agreed upon, and another engineer can implement it without further product or solution decisions.
- Use `Triage` when implementation is likely within six months but the decision, scope, or solution is not fully settled.
- Keep an explicit Engineering ticket request in Engineering even when it is idea-stage.

## Project selection

Every ticket must use an existing project that is not completed, canceled, archived, or trashed. Resolve the project in this order:

1. Use the project explicitly named by the user.
2. Use a clearly relevant active project from the current work context.
3. For Roam work, use `Roam Discourse Graph plugin assorted tasks`.
4. For Obsidian work, use `Obsidian Discourse Graphs plugin assorted tasks`.
5. Otherwise, use `Engineering Ops assorted tasks`.

Confirm the selected project still exists, is active, and includes the Engineering team. Never create a project. If a user-specified project is missing, ambiguous, or inactive, ask the user for another project instead of silently substituting one.

## Labels and optional fields

- Inspect existing issue labels and apply every clearly relevant label.
- Never create a label or guess an uncertain label.
- Missing or uncertain labels do not block creation. After creation, tell the user when no label was applied or when label selection remained uncertain.
- Set priority only when the user or context makes it clear and useful.
- Do not set a cycle or release. CI/CD handles releases.

## Create or draft

Draft without changing Linear when the user asks for a draft, review, or rewrite. Create the ticket without an additional confirmation when the user explicitly asks to create it.

Before creation, resolve the current Engineering statuses, selected project, and existing labels. Create the issue once with its title, completed description, status, project, labels, and justified priority. If the result is ambiguous, search for the issue before retrying so a transient failure does not create a duplicate.

After creation, return the issue identifier, title, status, project, and link. Include the generated branch name when Linear returns one. Do not restate the full description unless the user asks.

# DG Engineering Writing Style

Write in a direct, concise, plainspoken style that preserves important context and qualification.

## Core style

- Lead with the relevant point and move quickly to the concrete question, request, or action.
- Prefer the shortest version that remains clear and preserves necessary nuance.
- Identify wording or missing context that is ambiguous or could be misconstrued. Resolve it when the intended meaning is clear; otherwise, flag it and ask for clarification.
- Use natural contractions and everyday wording. Avoid corporate jargon, inflated phrasing, and generic professional filler.
- Avoid em dashes as sentence-level punctuation. Use a period, comma, colon, semicolon, or parentheses to separate thoughts instead. Preserve em dashes only when they appear in exact quotations, titles, source text, or technical content supplied by the requester.
- When identifying a problem or disagreement, state it plainly and pivot toward clarification, resolution, criteria, or next steps.
- Prefer bullets for distinct points. When prose reads more naturally, keep paragraphs and sentences short; avoid run-on sentences.
- Ask one clear question when one will do. Combine related questions only when separating them would add needless length.

## Adapt to the channel

- For a quick reply or chat message, omit the greeting and sign-off when they add no value.
- For technical issues, describe the observed behavior, the relevant contrast or expectation, and the requested clarification or next step.
- For engineering tickets and technical documentation, apply these ASD-STE100-inspired principles:
  - Use one term consistently for each concept. Do not alternate between synonyms.
  - Put one primary action or idea in each sentence.
  - Prefer active voice when the actor is important.
  - Replace vague verbs such as "handle," "support," or "improve" with the specific behavior or result.

## Drafting rules

- Preserve facts, commitments, dates, names, links, and technical meaning supplied by the requester.
- Do not invent availability, decisions, commitments, or emotional language.
- Treat explicit directions such as "shorter," "warmer," "more forceful," "broader," or "one sentence" as overrides for the current draft.
- When the requester asks for alternatives, vary the framing or emphasis rather than making superficial synonym swaps.
- Return a ready-to-use draft first. Add explanation only when requested or when an ambiguity materially affects the wording.

Draft, not created.

**Title:** Obsidian-origin asset tokens that fail to import create empty Roam pages

**Team:** Engineering · **Status:** Triage · **Project:** Push and pull nodes between Roam and Obsidian · **Label:** Roam plugin

```markdown
## Problem

- When an Obsidian-origin asset cannot be copied into Roam storage, the import stage leaves its token unchanged. Roam reads `![[attachments/diagram.png]]` as a page reference, so the import adds a link to an empty page named after a vault path, and the user is told the import succeeded.
- Roam-origin tokens degrade cleanly, because the published token is a public Firebase URL that still renders. Only Obsidian-origin tokens create junk pages.
- Reachable today in three ways: an asset over the 6 MiB import cap, a download or upload that fails, and a node whose assets were never recorded at publication.

## Solution

- Decide what an unresolvable Obsidian token becomes in a Roam page, then apply it in `rewriteAssetLinks`.
- The obvious candidate, rendering the token as plain text so Roam creates no page, conflicts with re-import repair: `rewriteAssetLinks` resolves by matching link and wikilink forms in the text, so a token rendered inert is a token a later import can no longer rewrite once the asset is available.
- Resolving that conflict is the work. Either pick an inert form the rewriter still recognizes, or make re-import repair the block from the `FileReference` rows it already iterates rather than from the text.

## Done When

- Importing an Obsidian-origin node whose asset fails creates no new page in the graph.
- The block still shows the reader what was referenced.
- Re-importing after the asset becomes available restores the working embed, or the ticket records why it cannot and what replaces it.

## Out of Scope

- Telling the user which assets degraded. ENG-1877 covers that.
- Roam-origin tokens, which render from the origin graph's storage and need no change.

## Notes

- Introduced with the asset stage in ENG-2219 and documented in the `importNodeAssets.ts` module comment.
- The constraint to work within is the cross-app-assets spec requirement "An unresolvable asset degrades to its original reference", which exists so a later re-import can still resolve the token.
```

Triage rather than Backlog because the solution is not settled: the inert-rendering fix and the re-import-repair requirement pull against each other, and that call should be made before someone picks this up.

Look up `:create/user` before writing "X thinks", "per Joel", or any attributed quote. <roam uid="QowkWQTjg" refs="1"/>

Attribute the __position__ to the initials and the __block__ to its creator, and say the initials are your basis. <roam uid="zgFhSiYI6" refs="1"/>

# roam/agent guidelines <roam uid="XcDxM3AGm" refs="9"/>

- This is the **discourse-graphs team graph** (dg-team). It tracks product development, user research, and design knowledge for the Discourse Graphs project. Start orientation at [[🚪 Discourse graphs front page for team members]]. <roam uid="ZyEFQdPzy"/>
- Graph Ontology <roam uid="CkMv_I9Hu" heading="2"/>
  - This graph uses a discourse graph node grammar with typed nodes. Each node type has a title format that the Roam plugin uses for identification via regex. Nodes exist at two levels of formality: <roam uid="JZ-ERybz9"/>
    - **Full node pages** — titled with the type prefix (e.g., `[[ISS]] - description`). These are the primary knowledge units. <roam uid="Lr2QOC061"/>
    - **Candidate nodes** — blocks tagged with a candidate hashtag (e.g., `#iss-candidate`, `#res-candidate`). These are seedling ideas not yet promoted to full pages. <roam uid="IxTd36BlH"/>
  - Node Types: Knowledge <roam uid="iJARoph1H" heading="3"/>
    - **Question (QUE)** — the unknowns being explored through pilots and research. Format: `[[QUE]] - {content}`. Sections: Summary, Notes, Testable hypotheses, Snippets. <roam uid="9uXF_YcQQ"/>
    - **Hypothesis (HYP)** — proposed answers to questions; collect evidence for or against. Format: `[[HYP]] - {content}`. Candidate tag: `#hyp-candidate`. Sections: Rationale, Snippets, Requests for Experiments. <roam uid="jA0VLkwMY"/>
    - **Result (RES)** — a discrete observation from ongoing research, in past tense. Format: `[[RES]] - {content} - {Source}`. Candidate tag: `#res-candidate`. Sections: Summary, Grounding Context, Snippets. Properties: NodeFormality (Draft → ReadyForInternal → ReadyToShare → Published), Contributors. <roam uid="21s0GTu6p"/>
    - **Evidence (EVD)** — a discrete observation from a published dataset or experiment. Format: `[[EVD]] - {content} - {Source}`. Sections: Evidence Description, Snippets, Grounding Context, Centrality slider. <roam uid="zgYL5nVb4"/>
    - **Claim (CLM)** — an assertion about how discourse graphs work or should work. Format: `[[CLM]] - {content}`. Candidate tag: `#clm-candidate`. <roam uid="9SOQK_533"/>
    - **Source (SRC)** — a referenced publication or external resource. Format: `@{content}`. <roam uid="wenbahwqN"/>
    - **Theory (THE)** — a theoretical framework or model. Format: `[[THE]] - {content}`. <roam uid="UtoPH2BxJ"/>
  - Node Types: Product & UX <roam uid="e-gV24nNQ" heading="3"/>
    - **Function (FUN)** — a UX "use case": a specific situation where Discourse Graphs can be used to enhance the experience. Tool-agnostic in framing, but tied to a concrete user goal. Format: `[[FUN]] - {content}`. Properties: FunctionImportance, FunctionScoping. <roam uid="LjYlqRpUR"/>
    - **Flow (FLO)** — a set of interactions the user performs to accomplish a goal within a particular implementation of Discourse Graphs (Obsidian plugin, Roam plugin, tldraw, etc.). A Flow is the tool-specific instantiation of a Function/Use Case. Format: `[[FLO]] - {content}`. Sections: Description (Goal, Loom, brief description), Steps (Normal flow, Alt flows, Exceptions), Examples, Pain points. Properties: FlowStatus (💭 Hypothetical → 🗓️ Planned → 🤔 Experimental → 🚧 Bespoke → 🔨 Alpha → 🚀 Beta), FlowFrequency, FlowImpact. <roam uid="SVcbz9E3i"/>
    - **Artifact (ART)** — the features, workflows, and UI components we build to enable Flows and Use Cases (Functions). Parts of a system are prefixed with the system name (e.g., `[[ART]] - Roam DG/Query`). Format: `[[ART]] - {content}`. Properties: ArtifactType (Feature/Component or Workflow/Template), ArtStatus (🤔 Prospective → 🖇️ Bespoke → 🧪 Alpha → 🎯 Beta → 💎 Release → 🌐 External). <roam uid="71FJwPgwi"/>
    - **PainPoint (PAI)** — problems, friction, and bottlenecks in user experience. Format: `[[PAI]] - {content}`. Properties: Activity, Function, Flow, UserTool. <roam uid="zD3lBBh9A"/>
    - **Journey (JOU)** — a user journey across multiple functions/flows. Format: `[[JOU]] - {content}`. Sections: Description, Phases, Pain points, Notes. <roam uid="YmhUG6VJX"/>
    - **Activity (ACT)** — an action the user performs that is not specific to any particular tool or method (e.g., "synthesize literature," "discuss findings"). Activities sit upstream of tool-bound Flows and Use Cases. Format: `[[ACT]] - {content}`. <roam uid="1NcVa1g2X"/>
    - **UserPilot** — a specific user or pilot engagement. Format: `UserPilot/{content}`. Properties: User status, UserTool (Roam, Obsidian, Notion, tldraw), UserType (Alpha/Beta/Normie), Lead. <roam uid="5XUZyDshG"/>
    - **CaseStudy (CAS)** — a documented case study. Format: `[[CAS]] - {content}`. <roam uid="ceCyzY2Ei"/>
  - Node Types: Project Management <roam uid="L4Lo_4B1w" heading="3"/>
    - **Issue (ISS)** — a potential action item for development or research. Format: `[[ISS]] - {content}`. Candidate tag: `#iss-candidate`. Properties: Issue Status (🤔 Considering → 🗓️ Backlog → 🗓️ Planned → 🚀 Active → 💬 Awaiting Feedback → ➡ Sent To Linear → ✅ Complete → 🧊 Iced → ⏸️ On hold), Issue Type (🗳️ Feature Request, 📄 Template improvement, 🐞 Bug Report, 🔬 Research, 🏗️ DG team, 🛠️ Maintenance), Priority, Project, Function, Flow, Lead. <roam uid="jzczOjTM1"/>
    - **Project** — a research or development project. Format: `Project/{content}`. Properties: Project Status (🗓️ Backlog → 🗓️ Planned → 🚀 Active → ✅ Complete → 🧊 Iced → ⏸️ On hold), Priority. <roam uid="IwUFa4By7"/>
    - **Milestone** — a time-boxed delivery target. Format: `Milestone/{content}`. Properties: Milestone Status, Start/End Date, Priority. <roam uid="NCfJPwcoO"/>
  - Relation Types <roam uid="PZxB_Lim1" heading="3"/>
    - **Supports / Supported By** — Evidence or Result supports a Claim, Hypothesis, or Conclusion <roam uid="QLrw6Cikm"/>
    - **Opposes / Opposed By** — Evidence or Result contradicts a Claim, Hypothesis, or Conclusion <roam uid="RdGHvBjvu"/>
    - **Informs / Informed By** — Evidence, Result, or Claim informs a Question or Hypothesis; Question informs Hypothesis; Hypothesis informs Issue <roam uid="0TFxQSHzV"/>
    - **Reproduces / Reproduced By** — Evidence confirms other Evidence <roam uid="lZNpV65LF"/>
    - **Resolves / Is resolved by** — Result resolves an Issue <roam uid="BKCUPTVYB"/>
    - To query typed relations programmatically, use `mcp__discourse__get_relationships uid=…` (the `discourse` MCP) — it returns a node's Supports / Opposes / Informs / Reproduces / Resolves edges and their complements directly. See **Which MCP tool for which task** under Navigating. The `roam` MCP can't resolve typed relations; with it, fall back to following page references within node content and checking linked references. <roam uid="4uQA80UCZ"/>
- Navigating the Graph <roam uid="I5GtkN5Cn" heading="2"/>
  - Which MCP tool for which task <roam uid="0w3wW5Rny" heading="3"/>
    - Two MCP servers read this graph. Reach for the **`discourse`** server whenever a task depends on the discourse-node / relation grammar (typed nodes, typed relations, the ontology); use the **`roam`** server for general text search, reading arbitrary pages, and all writes. <roam uid="v7YWcac84"/>
    - **Find discourse nodes by topic** → `mcp__discourse__search_nodes` (all query words must appear in the node title; optional `node_type_format` regex restricts to one type, e.g. `\[\[FLO\]\]` for Flows). For free-text across __all__ blocks — meeting notes, daily notes, non-node content — use `mcp__roam__search` instead. <roam uid="OmYGreM1F"/>
    - **List every node of a type** (all Flows, all Issues, …) → `mcp__discourse__get_all_discourse_nodes` (optional `since` ISO date for "what's new"). More reliable than a roam prefix search, which can miss nodes. <roam uid="OMwgWxWHS"/>
    - **Read a node's full content** → `mcp__discourse__get_node uid=…` for the title + full block tree; `mcp__roam__get_page` / `mcp__roam__get_block` are the general-purpose equivalents. <roam uid="2LarSnz-g"/>
    - **Find a node's typed relations** (what Supports / Opposes / Informs / Reproduces / Resolves it) → `mcp__discourse__get_relationships uid=…`. Resolves the typed edges directly; the roam server cannot. <roam uid="GS3OMHszL"/>
    - **Walk a node's neighborhood** (multi-hop reference graph) → `mcp__discourse__get_node_neighborhood uid=… depth=1–4 direction=both`. <roam uid="ur9V-QLL7"/>
    - **Get the live ontology** (node types + relation definitions) → `mcp__discourse__get_discourse_node_types`. The source of truth behind the **Graph Ontology** section above — pull it when you suspect the documented types or relations have drifted. <roam uid="qVG4hiqaO"/>
    - **General text search, recency, reading arbitrary pages, and all writes** → the **`roam`** server: `mcp__roam__search` (empty query = recently edited / viewed), `get_page`, `get_block`, `get_backlinks`, `create_block`, `update_block`. The `discourse` server is read-only. <roam uid="Tf4JXJyRu"/>
    - **Read the publication behind an `@source`** → check its `metadata::` / `Abstract::` block first; for full text use the `zotero` MCP (`mcp__zotero__*`) when it's in the user's Zotero library. <roam uid="wsMfcY8Rf"/>
    - **Find who created a block** → `mcp__roam__datalog_query` on `:create/user`. There is no dedicated block-author tool on either MCP server; this query is the only reliable way to get block-level provenance. Always bind it to a page or a uid — unbounded, it returns every block in the graph. <roam uid="YemilM2pX" refs="1"/>
      - By page: `[:find ?uid ?creator ?editor :in $ ?page-title :where [?p :node/title ?page-title] [?b :block/page ?p] [?b :block/uid ?uid] [?b :create/user ?cu] [?cu :user/display-page ?cp] [?cp :node/title ?creator] [?b :edit/user ?eu] [?eu :user/display-page ?ep] [?ep :node/title ?editor]]` — returns uid + names only. Don't add `?b :block/string ?s` unless you need it: it re-returns the whole page you already read, roughly 7x the tokens. <roam uid="7BKClr9BK" refs="1"/>
      - For a single block, replace the two page clauses with `[?b :block/uid ?uid]` and pass the uid as the input. <roam uid="icLRn-ci0" refs="1"/>
    - **Find who created a page or discourse node** → `mcp__discourse__get_node uid=…` returns `author`, `author_uid`, `created`, `modified`. Page-level only — given a __block__ uid it returns the content with no author, so fall back to the datalog query above. <roam uid="wRmrVnFqO" refs="1"/>
    - **List every identity in the graph** → `mcp__discourse__get_users` — humans, bots, and API tokens with their uids. Resolve a partial name here before making any authorship claim. <roam uid="7IXa9Yq2g" refs="1"/>
    - **See what one person wrote recently** → `mcp__discourse__catch_me_up author="…" days=N`. Needs the exact display name from `get_users`. <roam uid="0gEBMNuKz" refs="1"/>
    - **Find the discourse nodes a person authored** → `mcp__discourse__get_researcher_contributions author="…"`. Node __pages__ only — it returns 0 for identities that write blocks but never create node pages, so a 0 is not evidence that someone wrote nothing. <roam uid="0OshhlAu4" refs="1"/>
    - **Filter an existing query by author** → `mcp__discourse__run_discourse_query query_uid=…` honors the query builder's `created by` / `edited by` conditions. <roam uid="MyIALn-lG" refs="1"/>
    - On every call, pass the graph explicitly (`graph="dg-team"`) — several graphs are configured, and the wrong one silently returns nothing. <roam uid="STWu7JWy_"/>
  - Entry point <roam uid="MHzuk97bt" heading="3"/>
    - Start from [[🚪 Discourse graphs front page for team members]], which orients you to the main dashboards, functions/flows, pilot status, and hypotheses/results. <roam uid="nPt2-iVnj"/>
  - Following page references for context <roam uid="h9NTRhMjK" heading="3"/>
    - Much of a node's meaning lives in its **page references** — the `[[double-bracketed]]` links within its content blocks. These connect nodes to the Functions, Flows, Projects, Sources, and UserPilots that give them context. <roam uid="U28zLlsXL"/>
    - When reading a node, expand or follow its page references to understand **why** it exists and **what** it connects to. For example, a Result node's title includes its Source (e.g., `[[RES]] - users synthesized 3x more claims - [[@pilotStudy2025]]`), and its body may reference the Function or Flow it relates to. <roam uid="BQMJ8e_-z"/>
    - **Linked references** (at the bottom of any page) show every block in the graph that mentions that page. This is the primary way to see how a node is used in context — meeting notes, update logs, other discourse nodes, and daily notes entries. <roam uid="G9z0oYOKm"/>
    - **Block references** work similarly for individual blocks (bullets). If a block has a reference count, it has been cited elsewhere. <roam uid="Dcv_AHP0W"/>
  - Search strategies <roam uid="uDgL2s89Q" heading="3"/>
    - Search for discourse nodes by their type prefix: `[[QUE]] -`, `[[ISS]] -`, `[[FLO]] -`, `[[RES]] -`, etc. <roam uid="z9FqVtbYA"/>
    - Search for candidate nodes by their tag: `#iss-candidate`, `#res-candidate`, `#hyp-candidate`, `#clm-candidate`, `#flow-candidate`, `#up-candidate`, `#pro-candidate`. <roam uid="R6ZQgo7E-"/>
    - Search with empty query to see recently edited and viewed content — useful for understanding current activity. <roam uid="aHXgbk2iE"/>
    - For attributes with constrained values (status fields, priorities, tools, etc.), refer to [[roam/js/attribute-select]] for the canonical set of options. <roam uid="MaJPh5WXZ"/>

content.text:
Yes, it's scope creep, and the "easy" part is the half that doesn't pay.

Answering without touching anything:

**The one-line change is easy.** `mirrorAssetToRoamStorage` already computes `info?.contentType || blob.type` for the upload filename, so returning it on `MirroredAsset` is one field.

**But it only fires on the first import.** `ReusedAsset` comes from the registry, and `AssetRegistry` is `Record<string, string>` — hash to URL, nothing else. So a re-sync of the same node gets no mimetype.

That asymmetry is worse than the gap it closes. Take the case the finding cites, a Roam-origin storage URL with no recorded `source_path`:

- First import: `mirrored`, mimetype `image/png` present, `kindOf` returns `image`, block renders `![](url)`.
- Re-sync: `reused`, no mimetype, no extension on the uid, form is `bare`, so `kindOf` falls to `file` and the block renders `[abc123](url)`.

The same node would render differently depending on whether this graph had seen the asset before, and re-syncing would silently downgrade a working image embed to a link. Today's behaviour is wrong in one consistent way; the partial fix makes it wrong in a way that changes under the user's feet.

**Doing it properly spans three tickets.** The registry value has to carry the mimetype alongside the URL, which is ENG-2216's format and design.md Decision 4's `hash -> url` shape. Then 2218 returns it, then 2219 threads it into `ResolvedAsset`. Landing that in 2218 means editing a format ENG-2216 defined and adding a field 2218 has no consumer for — exactly what a scope check flags.

**My recommendation:** leave 2218 alone and file it as one small follow-up covering all three steps together, since only the whole chain is worth anything. It's a modest ticket: widen the registry value to `{ url, mimetype? }` with a read that tolerates the old string form, return the mimetype from the mirror, populate `ResolvedAsset`. The rewriter already names mimetype as its highest-fidelity signal, so nothing downstream changes.

Want that drafted as another issue candidate?

content.text:
Fixed, and the shared-matcher framing is the right one — my `spellingsOf` was the drift, not a smaller version of it.

`spellingsOf` is gone. `rewriteAssetLinks` now exports `collectAssetTokens`, and both it and the replacer read matches through one `parseMatch`, so the tokens a caller can see are by construction the tokens the rewriter will act on. The filter became:

```ts
const resolvable = new Set(collectAssetTokens(markdown).flatMap(lookupCandidates));
const referenced = references.filter(({ filepath }) => resolvable.has(filepath));
```

Same widening the rewrite uses, so a reference survives the filter exactly when the rewrite would resolve it. Nothing generates spellings forward any more, which is what made `#` and `?` a problem.

Worth being clear that this was a regression I introduced, not a pre-existing gap: before finding 5's filter every row was mirrored, and `lookupCandidates` decoded `fig%231.png` back to `fig#1.png` at rewrite time, so the image worked. My filter dropped it before the rewrite ever saw it — trading an over-copy for a silently missing image, which is the worse of the two.

New test covers it: recorded `fig#1.png`, markdown `![](fig%231.png)`, asserts one mirror call and the rewritten embed. 34 files / 299 tests pass, `tsc --noEmit` clean.

The refactor also removed the duplicated group destructuring from the replacer, so the branch ordering is now written down in exactly one place.

content.text:
This isn't one branch — it's an 8-deep stack of stacked PRs, each based on the one below:

```
#1390 eng-2229            -> main
#1392 eng-1864           -> eng-2229
#1394 eng-1870           -> eng-1864
#1395 eng-2230           -> eng-1870
#1402 eng-2216           -> eng-2230
#1397 eng-2218           -> eng-2216
#1398 eng-2217           -> eng-2218
#1401 eng-2219           -> eng-2217
```

Rebasing `eng-2219` onto main by itself would replay all 15 commits, flatten the stack into one PR diff, and break every base link below it. The real operation is bottom-up: `eng-2229` onto main, then each branch onto its rebuilt parent — 8 rewritten branches, all with open PRs.

The conflict surface is real either way. Main's 6 commits touch `materializeSharedNode.ts`, `importSharedNodes.ts`, `refreshImportedNode.ts`, `importedSourceIdentity.ts`, `Export.tsx`, `publishNodesToGroups.ts` and two of their test files — the same files this stack rewrote, and ENG-2156 and ENG-1861 both edited materialization directly.

options.label: Whole stack, bottom-up (recommended)
options.description: Rebase eng-2229 onto main, then each branch onto its rebuilt parent, through eng-2219. Preserves every PR's base link and keeps each PR's diff scoped to its own change. Rewrites 8 published branches, so it needs force-pushes afterwards, which I'd leave to you.

options.label: Only eng-2219 onto main
options.description: One rebase of 15 commits. Fastest to a working branch, but #1401's diff becomes the entire stack and the seven PRs below it lose their base chain.

options.label: Merge main into eng-2219 instead
options.description: One conflict resolution, no history rewrite, no force-push, other PRs untouched. Leaves a merge commit in the branch and doesn't help the other seven branches.

options.label: Leave config alone
options.description: I resolve each recurrence by hand. Slower, and risks the same conflict resolved two slightly different ways at different levels.

content.text:
Done. All eight branches rebased bottom-up, every one descends from main, and `pnpm ci:validate` passes on each.

**Three conflicts, all real ones:**

1. `publishNodesToGroups.test.ts` (ENG-1870 task 2.4) — both sides rewrote the fake Supabase client. Main's ENG-1968 builder added `url.search`/`order`/`range` for its pre-check; ours added `delete` support and an awaitable `eq` chain. Main's builder already satisfies what `publishNodeAssets` needs from `select` (chaining `eq`, awaitable on its own), so I kept it and added our `deleteFilter` and `delete:` entry. Comment in place saying why.
2. `materializeSharedNode.ts` (ENG-2219) — main's ENG-2156 renamed the create/update title argument to `pageTitle` (core_title decoration). Kept our asset flow, `markdown` from the stage and `assets: report` on success, using main's `pageTitle`.
3. `materializeSharedNode.test.ts` + two import blocks — main appended seven decoration tests immediately before the same anchor our two stage tests went before, so both blocks are kept in order. The import conflicts were mechanical: main added `resolveSharedNodeTypes`, we split `getErrorMessage` into its own module; both imports now present.

`rerere` earned its keep on the import-block conflicts and recorded resolutions for all three, so a repeat of this rebase replays them.

**Old → new tips:**

```
eng-2229  20f5362c8 -> a34e4cc84      eng-2216  2a3ca2f5c -> bc186d04f
eng-1864  36e0ff10d -> a243f7cab      eng-2218  23e7946b3 -> bbe967478
eng-1870  7839b4c94 -> 264ccb538      eng-2217  e0588dd46 -> 0f5a93eaa
eng-2230  4831cd188 -> 712185828      eng-2219  06a464c56 -> 1043e32ff
```

Every old tip is saved at `refs/prerebase/<branch>`, so `git reset --hard refs/prerebase/eng-2219-…` restores any branch exactly. Delete them with `git for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' refs/prerebase | xargs -n1 git update-ref -d` once you're satisfied.

**Left for you:** the force-pushes, in bottom-up order so each PR's base exists before its child updates:

```
for b in eng-2229-add-a-filename-column-to-filereference \
         eng-1864-define-cross-app-asset-reference-contract \
         eng-1870-copy-roam-origin-assets-into-supabase-on-publish \
         eng-2230-split-filepath-and-source_path-across-obsidian-publish-and \
         eng-2216-Add-a-graph-level-asset-registry-accessor-for-Roam \
         eng-2218-Copy-assets-from-supabase-into-Roam-storage \
         eng-2217-rewrite-asset-links-in-obsidian-origin-markdown-for-roam \
         eng-2219-add-an-asset-copy-stage-to-roam-node-materialization
do git push --force-with-lease origin "$b"; done
```

The base branch of each PR is unchanged, so GitHub keeps the chain and each diff stays scoped to its own change. I also set `rerere.enabled` and `rerere.autoupdate` in this repo's local config — say if you'd rather I unset them.

You're back on `eng-2219-…` with a clean tree.
